meta.title: Stepper-motor driver with trapezoidal acceleration
meta.tools: C firmware (full/half-step sequencing, Austin's real-time ramp algorithm) on the simulated MCU
meta.summary: Drive a 200-step/rev stepper through a 3-revolution move with a trapezoidal speed profile computed in real time (David Austin's c_n recurrence); decode step timing from the pin log and compare the velocity profile and move time with kinematics.
meta.problem: Steppers stall if you ask them to start at full speed. How does firmware generate an accurate acceleration ramp using only integer-friendly arithmetic?
meta.theory:
For acceleration α (steps/s²) the first step delay is $c_0=\sqrt{2/\alpha}$ and subsequent delays follow $c_n=c_{n-1}-\frac{2c_{n-1}}{4n+1}$ (Austin 2005),
approximating the exact $c_n = \sqrt{2/\alpha}(\sqrt{n+1}-\sqrt n)$. Trapezoid: accelerate to v_max over $v_{max}^2/(2\alpha)$ steps, cruise, decelerate
symmetrically. Move time = $\frac{S}{v_{max}}+\frac{v_{max}}{\alpha}$ when the cruise phase exists. Half-stepping doubles resolution (400 steps/rev).
meta.method:
S = 1,200 half-steps (3 rev), α = 4,000 steps/s², v_max = 2,000 steps/s. Coil outputs A, B, A̅, B̅ on 4 pins with the 8-state half-step table;
firmware schedules each step at the computed delay (1 µs resolution).

metrics.note: half-step table: A, AB, B, BĀ, Ā, ĀB̄, B̄, B̄A
